requirement:
The harness MUST expose a `habeas` tool accepting exactly one of these request
forms. Each form MUST correspond to one existing evidence-input kind:

| Request fields | Evidence input returned | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file: String`, `line_start: Integer`, optional `line_end: Integer` | Outline inputs for the innermost outline nodes covering the range | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `file: String`, `item: String` | Outline input | {cite}`requirements.ci.outline_inputs` |
| `requirements: String` | Requirements input, including its matching names | {cite}`requirements.ci.requirements_inputs` |
| `definition: String` | Definition input | {cite}`requirements.definitions.inputs` |

Selector arguments MUST use the syntax defined by
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Reads MUST use the current
project working tree, including unstaged changes to tracked files and staged new
files. By default, source inputs MUST stay within the project root after
resolving symlinks; in a Git worktree, both the requested file and its resolved
target MUST be present in the Git index. Projects outside Git MUST use the same
containment rules without requiring an index. Failure to read an existing
repository's index MUST be reported as an error.
The project-root `evidence/` directory and an active workspace configuration
containing literal credentials MUST be excluded from model reads by default,
including symlink aliases. Generated build outputs MUST follow
{cite}`requirements.authoring.generated_inputs`. Workspace path overrides MUST
follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.evidence_paths`, including explicit
permission for otherwise excluded inputs. A denied mandatory input or explicit
read MUST abort under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.

Line numbers are only a way to request sources; recorded evidence MUST identify
sources by outline selector and structural hash, never by line number. Request
line numbers MUST be one-based and inclusive, and omitting `line_end` MUST read
through EOF. A line-range request MUST be resolved to the innermost outline
nodes covering the requested lines, which are `line` nodes in a file using the
plain-text profile; the result MUST show the model each node's selector, current
line range, and source text, and the harness MUST record those nodes as outline
inputs. The model-facing tool description MUST include the argument conventions
from the cited requirements, including outline selector syntax, definition
selections, and full definition names, with a short request example for each form.

A successful call MUST return the requested evidence input, populated by the
harness with the selected source text, using the existing evidence schema.
{cite}`requirements.ci.schema`
Required terminology dependencies MUST be returned alongside it as additional
definition inputs under {cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.
The result MUST have this shape:

```text
HabeasResult {
    input: EvidenceInput,
    definitions: Array<DefinitionInput>,
}
```

`definitions` MUST be empty when no additional terminology is required. The
harness MUST record inputs supplied to the model in the assessment's evidence.
A failed read MUST add no evidence input. Access-policy denials MUST abort
except where {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial` makes them ordinary read
failures; other failed reads MUST return an explanatory tool error.
rationale:
**Judgment: the sources satisfy `requirements.authoring.source_tools`.**

**Implementation**

- **Four request forms.**
  - `tools::definitions` (`src/authoring/tools.rs:18`) advertises a single `habeas` tool with optional `file`, `line_start`, `line_end`, `item`, `requirements` and `definition` fields.
  - `tools::read` (`tools.rs:88`) enforces exactly one form. It rejects unknown, mixed and incomplete argument sets through `check_keys`, `string` and `integer`.
  - `file+line_start[+line_end]` goes through `read_lines` to `nodes_for_range` and `Outline::nodes_for_lines`. These resolve the innermost covering nodes and return `{inputs, definitions}`.
  - The other three forms go through `read_selector` and `source_input`, which return `{input, definitions}`.
  - Each form maps onto an existing evidence-input kind (outline, requirements, definition), using `InputSelector::to_model_input`. Model-facing inputs add `kind`, `line_start`, `line_end` and `text`. Recorded inputs carry only the selector and hash.
- **Line numbers.** Reads are one-based and inclusive. An omitted `line_end` defaults to EOF. Zero, inverted or out-of-range requests are errors. Recording goes by selector and hash, never by line number.
- **Tool description.** The description covers selector syntax (`kind[name]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `kind@hash`, `#N`, percent-encoding), definition selections, globs, full definition names and one example per form.
- **Source access.** `SourceAccess::path` and `tracked_sources` (`src/authoring/access.rs`) implement the access rules:
  - Reads use the working tree, with Git index membership required for both the requested path and its resolved symlink target. Projects outside Git skip the index check, and an index that cannot be read is reported as an error.
  - Project containment is checked after symlink resolution.
  - `evidence/` and a workspace config containing credentials are excluded by default, including through symlink aliases.
  - Explicit allow and disallow rules, and discovered Cargo build-script output directories, follow `evidence_paths` and `generated_inputs`.
- **Denial and failure handling.**
  - Policy denials abort (`assess` in `src/authoring/mod.rs` returns on `PermissionDenied`).
  - Ordinary read failures, malformed arguments and unpermitted out-of-project paths become explanatory tool errors, via `OutsideProject`, `recoverable_outside_request` and `recoverable_os_denial`.
  - A failed read adds no inputs, because `ToolDelivery` is built only on success.
- **Terminology and recording.** `additional_definitions` supplies the required terminology transitively. Delivered inputs are recorded only after the next successful provider response, in `assess`.
- **Marking.** Implementing code carries `{impl}` markers. The one cite-only site is the plain `SourceAccess` struct declaration at `access.rs:88`. It holds state but has no behavior, and the functions that act on it are all marked `{impl}`, so I don't count it as a gap.

**Tests**

- **Tool surface.** `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` (`tools.rs`) covers all four forms, EOF line ranges, out-of-range and zero lines, missing items, and ten malformed or mixed argument sets. `habeas_tool_describes_its_argument_conventions_with_an_example_per_form` checks the description. `line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes` covers the range-to-node resolution and that recorded inputs hold only selector and hash.
- **Git index.** `access.rs` and `inputs.rs` tests cover nested projects, an unreadable or invalid index failing hard, an empty `.git` in an ancestor, and mandatory inputs needing staging. The `tools.rs` tests cover staged and dirty files, untracked files, and symlinks needing both alias and target tracked.
- **Excluded paths.** `generated_evidence_is_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery`, `outside_symlinks_are_excluded_from_reads_search_and_discovery` and `workspace_credentials_are_excluded_unless_explicitly_allowed` cover the default exclusions, including symlink aliases.
- **Allow, disallow and generated outputs.** Tests cover allow overriding defaults with disallow winning over aliases and ancestors. They also cover Cargo `OUT_DIR` discovery without a build, the inherited `OUT_DIR` being ignored, and metadata failure.
- **Abort versus recoverable.** `unpermitted_requests_outside_the_project_are_recoverable_tool_errors` and the CLI test `explicit_untracked_reads_abort_without_another_request_or_evidence_write` check abort against recoverable behavior. The CLI test also checks no evidence write and the usage record. The Bedrock CLI test checks the provider schema and the recorded outline inputs.

Remaining untested edge cases are minor and do not warrant a gap.

The result MUST have this shape:
```text
HabeasResult {
input: EvidenceInput,
definitions: Array<DefinitionInput>,
`definitions` MUST be empty when no additional terminology is required. The
harness MUST record inputs supplied to the model in the assessment's evidence.
A failed read MUST add no evidence input. Access-policy denials MUST abort
except where {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial` makes them ordinary read
failures; other failed reads MUST return an explanatory tool error.
:::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} requirements_inputs

For a requirements input, `requirements` MUST be a {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`, and Habeas MUST match it against all defined requirements and named examples. It MUST recompute the matches during validation, sort their full names, and compare them with `matches`. It MUST take each match's complete raw fenced declaration, including its opening and closing lines, concatenate those declarations in full-name order with one blank line between them, and compare the resulting raw lines with `text`. It MUST retain every match's current source file and inclusive line range for display and reference coverage. A selection matching no definitions MUST be invalid. Adding, removing, renaming, or changing a matched definition MUST invalidate the stored input; moving an unchanged declaration within the book MUST NOT. Errors MUST identify the selection and affected definitions when available.
:::{req} inputs

Evidence inputs MAY have a definition form containing exactly `definition` and `text`. `definition` MUST identify one named definition; `text` MUST contain its complete raw fenced declaration as source lines, including its phrase option and explanatory body.

Validation MUST reject missing definitions and changed snapshot text, identifying the definition and showing a compact diff when available. Moving an unchanged definition within its chapter MUST NOT invalidate its snapshot. Evidence displays MUST show the definition name, current source location, and recorded text.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} generated_inputs
Habeas MUST permit existing Cargo build-script output directories as an exception
to default Git tracking and containment restrictions. It MUST discover the Cargo
build directory using metadata and inspect existing build-script output records,
without running a build or executing build scripts. It MUST NOT treat its own
inherited `OUT_DIR` environment variable as the workspace's output directory.
Only discovered output directories and their contents MUST receive this default
permission; unrelated build artifacts MUST remain subject to ordinary rules.
Workspace disallow entries MUST override this permission.
Discovery MUST tolerate missing builds or unavailable metadata; callers MUST be
able to allow undiscovered outputs explicitly using `habeas.toml`. The model's
root directory listing MUST expose available generated-output directories,
including external ones. Generated inputs MUST use outline inputs and receive
ordinary freshness checks. Validation MUST NOT
invoke a build to materialize an input.
:::{req} evidence_paths
The workspace `[evidence]` table MUST serialize EvidenceConfig. `allow` and
`disallow` MUST be arrays of nonempty literal paths, each naming a file or a
directory subtree. Relative paths MUST resolve from the selected `habeas.toml`
directory; absolute paths MUST be supported. These paths are not glob patterns.
An omitted `allow` or `disallow` MUST mean an empty array, and an absent
`[evidence]` table MUST mean both are empty, so only the default source-access
rules apply. No operation requires the section. The table has no user-file
counterpart, and these rules have no invocation options. This section refines
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the evidence feature.
For authoring reads, a matching disallow MUST reject the path; otherwise a
matching allow MUST permit it; otherwise the default source-access rules MUST
apply. Explicit allow MUST override every default, including Git tracking,
project containment, generated-evidence exclusion, and automatic generated-output
rules. Disallow MUST win even when an allow or generated-output rule also matches.
Both the requested path and its resolved symlink target MUST be checked for
disallow, so an allowed alias cannot expose a disallowed target.
The same explicit disallow rules and external-path exceptions MUST apply when
resolving recorded evidence inputs, including ordinary validation and
`add-input`. Validation MUST remain independent of Git index membership: it
checks the recorded inputs' existence and contents. Loading path policy MUST NOT
resolve credentials or validate unused authoring settings.
:::{req} read_denial
When a mandatory input or dispatched model read is denied by source-access
policy, the assessment MUST abort and report the denied path and reason to its caller.
It MUST NOT return the denial to the model as a recoverable tool result or make
another model request for that assessment. An untracked-file diagnostic MUST
explain that the caller can stage the file with `git add` or configure a workspace
allow rule; the harness MUST NOT stage or permit the file itself.
The aborted assessment MUST NOT write evidence or emit evidence JSON. Its usage
record MUST identify the failure and any failed tool call. In a batch, other
assessments MUST continue, including queued assessments, and their successful
writes MUST be retained. The command MUST return a nonzero exit status after
the batch finishes. Discovery and search MAY omit denied candidates without
aborting, but explicitly requesting a denied file or directory MUST abort the
affected assessment.
Malformed tool arguments and ordinary read failures MUST retain their existing
recoverable tool-error behavior.
A dispatched model request naming a path outside the project root, before
symlinks are resolved, that no workspace allow rule or generated-output rule
permits MUST be treated as an ordinary read failure rather than an abort: it
MUST return an explanatory tool error, add no evidence input, and let the
assessment continue. An explicit workspace disallow matching such a path MUST
still abort. A mandatory input naming such a path, and a request inside the
project whose symlink target leaves it, MUST still abort.
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
